issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies Animal has a constructor Animal(String, int) (name and age), but the provided solution implements Animal with a single-parameter constructor Animal(String). This mismatch in constructor parameters conflicts with the UML/specification and would confuse students about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the problem statement/UML to require only a single-argument constructor Animal(String) (and remove the age attribute), or change the solution/template to implement Animal with both name and age fields and a constructor Animal(String, int) plus getters/setters for both attributes so the implementation matches the UML.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Animal has an attribute 'age: int', but the solution's Animal class contains only a 'name' attribute and omits 'age'. This attribute mismatch between specification and solution is structural and may mislead students about which fields are required.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and implementation: add an 'age' field of type int to Animal in the solution and template, provide appropriate getter/setter methods, and ensure the constructor initializes both name and age (or revise the UML/specification to remove the age attribute if it is not intended).

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and task text specify that Animal has an 'age' attribute and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the provided solution and template code use a single-argument constructor Animal(String) and do not provide an 'age' field. This mismatch between the documented API (Animal(String,int) and 'age') and the implemented API (Animal(String) with no age) creates confusion for students trying to map the UML/tasks to the code and to the expected subclass constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal API consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution and template code to implement the 'age' attribute and constructor Animal(String, int) (add private int age, getter/setter, and change subclass constructors to call super(name, age) and adjust Main usages), or update the problem statement/UML to specify only a single-argument constructor Animal(String) and remove the 'age' attribute from the UML and tasks so all artifacts agree.
